transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-21 16:00 PST | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jason Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Torres (Aurora Head of ML), Samir Desai (Aurora Infra), Priya Rao (Aurora CISO)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Jason's our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Jason Patel: Hi all, thanks. We'll jump into the Console, focus on the usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and then the cost breakdown. Happy to take questions as we go.
[00:17] Lena Torres: Great, we're mostly interested in how cost maps to routes — we have two main services, a user-facing chat and a nightly summarization batch.
[00:26] Samir Desai: And from infra, we want to understand burst behavior and how dedicated capacity would change unit costs.
[00:33] Priya Rao: Security first — SOC2, KMS, VPC peering, and audit logs. We'll need clear answers there.
[00:40] Jason Patel: Totally. I'll start by sharing my screen — Console > Analytics > Usage.
[00:48] [screen share noise / rustle]
[00:52] Jason Patel: So here is the top-level tokens/time series — you can filter by model, route, environment. This chart is token consumption over time, and here's a per-route breakdown.
[01:05] Jason Patel: Notice the route table on the right — each route shows avg latency, p50/p95, token count, and cost per 1k tokens, which is calculated from model profile + infra.
[01:18] Lena Torres: That cost per route math, is that assuming hosted with on-demand or reserved/dedicated pricing?
[01:24] Jason Patel: Good call — by default it shows hosted on-demand. You can switch the cost model dropdown to "Dedicated" or upload your reserved commit numbers and we'll re-compute the unit economics.
[01:35] Maya Chen: Also we provide a compare view so you can see hosted vs. dedicated side-by-side for the same time window.
[01:42] Samir Desai: When you say "re-compute", what about quantization and batching assumptions — do you assume 4-bit quantized models by default?
[01:51] Jason Patel: There's a profile tied to each model variant — by default it's the verified runbook we published; it includes typical quantization (int8 or int4 depending on model), batching envelope, and KV cache hit assumptions. You can override those parameters per evaluation.
[02:05] Priya Rao: The KV cache, sorry — I sometimes see it written as K V in transcripts, but we mean key-value cache for conversational state, right?
[02:13] Jason Patel: Yes, KV cache for chat. The Console surfaces cache hit rate, which is a huge lever for lowering tokens and latency.
[02:20] [00:02 pause - mouse click]
[02:23] Jason Patel: Here's the per-route drilldown for your chat route — you can see tokens per call distribution, median response size, and the per-route cost bucketed by model and by infra tier.
[02:36] Lena Torres: Can we toggle to show only p95 latency and cost attribution to model vs infra?
[02:41] Jason Patel: Yep, top right is the metric selector. Switching to p95 and cost attribution now.
[02:46] [short pause, typing]
[02:50] Jason Patel: OK — see the stacked bars: model compute cost, memory overhead (NVMe, etc), and network egress. We attribute token compute to model cost and GPU-hours to infra cost, so you can see where optimizations help.
[03:05] Lena Torres: For our nightly summarization, latency isn't critical but cost is. For chat it's the opposite. How would you recommend splitting models or routes?
[03:15] Jason Patel: Typical approach is dual model variants — a cheaper distilled/quantized model for batch/summarize, and a higher-capacity model for chat. Console lets you route by policy (latency, cost, user tier) and fall back automatically if capacity is constrained.
[03:30] Maya Chen: And you can pin model versions per route during rollouts so the production chat route stays stable.
[03:35] Samir Desai: On Dedicated — how much does cost drop for sustained throughput? Any back-of-envelope?
[03:41] Maya Chen: For a sustained commit, it's usually 30-55% lower per-token than hosted on-demand depending on model family and utilization. We'll send a tailored estimate based on your traffic profile.
[03:52] Samir Desai: Cool. Can you show the historical cost explorer?
[03:55] Jason Patel: Sure — Console > Cost Explorer. You can group by route, model, or tag. Here I group by route and see the chat route accounts for ~72% of your daily token spend.
[04:07] Jason Patel: There's also a forecast tab which projects next 30 days under current usage and under optimized batching/kv cache settings.
[04:15] Lena Torres: The forecast — how sensitive is it to batch size assumptions? Our peak concurrency varies.
[04:20] Jason Patel: It's quite sensitive; the forecast allows you to set percentiles for concurrency and we show the effect on batching efficiency and expected cost.
[04:29] Priya Rao: Security questions — where are logs stored, and how long? Are audit logs HIPAA-ready?
[04:36] Maya Chen: Audit logs are available with our enterprise plan; retention and export are configurable. We have SOC 2 Type II; for HIPAA we offer BAAs and can discuss entitlements for log retention in the Private deployment.
[04:51] Priya Rao: KMS integration? Customer-managed keys?
[04:54] Jason Patel: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations and key rotation. For hosted, we provide envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS in VPC Private deployments.
[05:07] Priya Rao: SSO and RBAC?
[05:09] Maya Chen: SSO via SAML/SCIM; role-based access control is in the Console and we can map groups to routes and actions.
[05:17] Samir Desai: Any gotchas around VPC peering? We run in GCP and have strict egress rules.
[05:24] Jason Patel: We support VPC peering and private link; network egress can be minimized with regional endpoints. We'll include a network design note in the follow-up.
[05:33] [background murmurs]
[05:37] Lena Torres: One operational question — how do we set alerts for cost anomalies per route?
[05:42] Jason Patel: Alerts live in the Console Alerts page — you can set thresholds or anomaly detection on tokens/spend/latency per route. We also send daily digest emails and can integrate with PagerDuty/Slack.
[05:55] Lena Torres: Nice. For the pilot, can we get the per-route report exported as CSV with model labels and cost columns?
[06:03] Jason Patel: Yep, export button top-right -> CSV/JSON. You can also schedule automated exports.
[06:11] [short crosstalk]
[06:15] Priya Rao: About procurement — do you support purchase orders and enterprise contracts?
[06:20] Maya Chen: Yes, we've got enterprise agreements, monthly/annual reserved capacity contracts, and PO-friendly invoicing.
[06:27] Samir Desai: If we run the 2-week pilot on hosted, can we later move to Dedicated with minimal changes?
[06:33] Jason Patel: Yes, the API and routes are the same. The difference is capacity planning and config — we help with migration tooling; most customers transition without code changes.
[06:43] Lena Torres: Any mention of competitors in your benchmarks? We care about quality vs cost — people compare Anthropic and OpenAI a bunch.
[06:49] Jason Patel: We include curated benchmarks and open model profiles; we also publish Redwood-verified perf numbers. We can run a side-by-side on your prompts during the pilot if you want.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Quick recap before we wrap: we'll send pricing + Dedicated estimate, security docs (SOC 2, KMS integration, network design), and Jason will prep pilot runbook and sample telemetry dashboard. Samir will share traffic patterns and SSO metadata.
[07:14] Priya Rao: Sounds good. Can we get an NDA or any legal forms before exchanging sensitive logs?
[07:20] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll loop in legal and send the NDA and any required docs.
[07:25] [end screen share]
[07:28] Jason Patel: One more demo note — Console Optimize suggestions show batch/caching changes and expected cost delta. For your chat route, we estimate 12-18% savings by tweaking batching and prefix caching.
[07:40] Lena Torres: We'll take that.
[07:42] Maya Chen: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.
[07:48] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — some model names and acronyms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., K V cache -> KV cache, quantization labels).

References / Links mentioned: Console Analytics (link placeholder), Pricing spreadsheet (to be sent), SOC 2 report (to be sent), Pilot runbook (to be sent).
